sentences.text: Shri Arvind Singh - Government Advocate for the respond Heard on I.A. 18740/2023, which is an application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant Lavkush Patel.

B y impugned judgment dated 30/6/2023 passed by the Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences) Act, Anuppur Distt. Anuppur (M.P.) in Special Case No.64/2020 the appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 450 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs. 1,000/-, Section 376 (2)(N) of the IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years with fine of Rs. 2,000/- and also Section 5(L)/6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years with fine of Rs. 2,000/- respectively with default stipulations.

entities.text: Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences) Act, Anuppur Distt. Anuppur (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant by taking this Court to the prosecution story submits that first incident of sexual assault is allegedly happened on 10/10/2015, when both the prosecutrix and the appellant were minor.
This is a case of continuous romantic relationship which continued even after the prosecutrix become major.
FIR has been lodged on 20/10/2020 near about 5 years of the date of first incident of sexual assault.
He also submits that it is not a case of sexual exploitation on the ground of false promise of marriage.

To bolster, he has placed heavy reliance on the para 18 of the judgment passed in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and anoter,
(2019) 9 SCC 608.

sentences.text: The appellant has remained in custody during trial for about 5 months and after passing the judgment on 30/6/2023, he is in jail.
DNA report is negative.
Statements of the prosecution witnesses have material omissions and contradictions.
The final hearing of this matter is not possible in near future.
Thus, remaining jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended.
The prayer is opposed by learned Government Advocate on the basis of objection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.

Considering the factual backdrop and bleak chances of final hearing in near future, without expressing any conclusive opinion on the merits of the case, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of Lavkush Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84072046/
1 appellant.
Accordingly, I.A. No.18740/2023 is allowed.
Subject to depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited), the remaining jail sentence of appellant is hereby suspended and it is directed that appellant Lavkush Patel be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court, Anuppur o n 12/2/2024 and also on such other dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
